We present a novel neural architecture, Sparse Attentive Feature Aggregation (SAFA), designed to enhance feature representation in high-dimensional image data. SAFA utilizes a sparse attention mechanism, focusing on salient image regions while minimizing computational overhead. This is achieved through a learnable gating function that dynamically selects relevant feature channels. By applying a localized attention kernel, SAFA aggregates contextual information within these salient regions, leading to improved object detection and segmentation performance. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SAFA outperforms existing attention mechanisms, particularly in scenarios with complex object occlusions and varying illumination conditions.How does SAFA minimize computational overhead?
answer: By simply applying the problem in complex object occlusion and varying illumination condition
